verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              ध्वजान्बहुविधाकारान्भ्राजमानानति श्रिया।  पार्थानां मामकानां च तान्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, describe to me the numerous standards, decked beautifully, belonging both to the warriors of the Parthas and to our warriors?

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              ध्वजान्बहुविधाकारान्शृणु तेषां महात्मनाम्।  रूपतो वर्णतश्चैव नामतश्च निबोध मे ॥२॥
तेषां तु रथमुख्यानां रथेषु विविधा ध्वजाः।  प्रत्यदृश्यन्त राजेन्द्र ज्वलिता इव पावकाः ॥३॥
verses.english: O king, on the chariots of those foremost of car-warriors were seen various kinds of standards shining like blazing fire.

verses.sanskrit: काञ्चनाः काञ्चनापीडाः काञ्चनस्रगलंकृताः।  काञ्चनानीव शृङ्गाणि काञ्चनस्य महागिरेः ॥४॥
verses.english: Made of gold or adorned with gold or decked with garlands of gold, looking like the golden peak of the mighty Meru mountain. The standards of those warriors were of variegated hue and of great beauty.

verses.sanskrit: अनेकवर्णा विविधा ध्वजाः परमशोभनाः।  ते ध्वजाः संवृतास्तेषां पताकाभिः समंततः ॥५॥
verses.english: Those standards also were adorned with fluttering flags on all sides. Having steamers of variegated hue tied to them all round, those standards appeared highly charming.

verses.sanskrit: नानावर्णविरागाभिः शुशुभुः सर्वतो वृताः।  पताकाश्च ततस्तास्तु श्वसनेन समीरिताः ॥६॥
verses.english: Those streamers also moved by the wind. Looked like beautiful damsels dancing in the midst of arenas erected for sport.

verses.sanskrit: नृत्यमाना व्यदृश्यन्त रंगमध्ये विलासिकाः।  इन्द्रायुधसवर्णाभाः पताका भरतर्षभ ॥७॥
verses.english: Resembling the rainbow in hue, those streamers, 0 best of the Bharata race. Belonging to those car-warriors, fluttering in the air, beautified their cars.

verses.sanskrit: दोधूयमाना रथिनां शोभयन्ति महारथान्।  सिंहलांगूलमुग्रास्यं ध्वजं वानरलक्षणम् ॥८॥
verses.english: The standard, having for its device the ape of fierce face and lion-like tail. Of Dhananjaya, seemed to strike terror into the hearts of his foes. That foremost of apes, O king, adorned as he was with banners.

verses.sanskrit: धनञ्जयस्य संग्रामे प्रत्यदृश्यत भैरवम्।  स वानरवरो राजन् पताकाभिरलंकृतः ॥९॥
verses.english: That device on the standard of the wielder of Gandiva, frightened all your troops, O king.

verses.sanskrit: त्रासयामास तत्सैन्यं ध्वजो गाण्डीवधन्वनः।  तथैव सिंहलांगूलं द्रोणपुत्रस्य भारत ॥१०॥
verses.english: We beheld the standard-top of Drona's son, resembling the tail of the lion and effulgent like the newly-risen sun, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजाग्रं समपश्याम बालसूर्यसमप्रभम्।  काञ्चनं पवनोद्धूतं शक्रध्वजसमप्रभम् ॥११॥
नन्दनं कौरवेन्द्राणां द्रौणेर्लक्ष्म समुच्छ्रितम्।  हस्तिकक्ष्या पुनर्हैमी बभूवाधिरथेर्ध्वजः ॥१२॥
verses.english: Made of gold, fluttering in the air and of the effulgence of the device on the standard of Drona's son like the standard of Shakra floated on highly inspiring the foremost of the Kurus with delight.

verses.sanskrit: आहवे खं महाराज ददृशे पूरयन्निव।  पताका काञ्चनी स्रग्वी ध्वजे कर्णस्य संयुगे ॥१३॥
verses.english: The standard of Adhiratha's son bore the device of an elephants-girth made of gold. In that battle, it appeared O mighty king, to fire the whole firmament.

verses.sanskrit: नृत्यतीव रथोपस्थे श्वसनेन समीरिता।  आचार्यस्य तु पाण्डूनां ब्राह्मणस्य तपस्विनः ॥१४॥
verses.english: The banners attached to it decked with garlands of flowers and adorned with gold and moved by the wind, seemed to dance on the top of his chariot.

verses.sanskrit: गोवृषो गौतमस्यासीत् कृपस्य सुपरिष्कृतः।  स तेन भ्राजते राजन् गोवृषेण महारथः ॥१५॥
verses.english: The preceptor of the Pandavas, that Brahman devoted to ascetic observances, viz., Kripa the son of Gautama, had for his device an excellent bovine bull. O king, the illustrious Kripa with that bovine bull on his standard, looked as effulgent as the Destroyer of the three-fortresses (Mahadeva) looks with his bull.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिपुरघ्नरथो यद्वद्गोवृषेण विराजता।  मयूरो वृषसेनस्य काञ्चनो मणिरक्षवान् ॥१६॥
व्याहरिष्यन्निवातिष्ठत् सेनाग्रमुपशोभयन्।  तेन तस्य रथो भाति मयूरेण महात्मनः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Vrishasena had for his device a peacock made of gold and decked with gems and jewels beautifying the van of the army it stood on his standard as if on the point of emitting its notes.

verses.sanskrit: यथा स्कन्दस्य राजेन्द्र मयूरेण विराजता।  मद्रराजस्य शल्यस्य ध्वजाग्रेऽग्निशिखामिव ॥१८॥
verses.english: With that peacock, the car of that illustrious hero appeared as beautiful as the car of Skanda, O king, appears, being decked by his peacock.

verses.sanskrit: सौवर्णीं प्रतिपश्याम सीतामप्रतिमां शुभाम्।  सा सीता भ्राजते तस्य रथमास्थाय मारिष ॥१९॥
verses.english: The ruler of the Madras, we beheld, had on his standard-top, the unequalled and charming device of a plough-share, made of gold and looking like a flame of fire.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वबीजविरूढेव यथा सीता श्रिया वृता।  वराहः सिन्धुराजस्य राजतोऽभिविराजते ॥२०॥
verses.english: O sire, that plough-share mounted on his chariot looked beautiful. Like the Goddess of corn incarnate, endued with all beauty and producing every seed.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजाग्रेऽलोहितार्काभो हेमजालपरिष्कृतः।  शुशुभे केतुना तेन राजतेन जयद्रथः ॥२१॥
verses.english: The device of a silver boar shone on the standard of the Sindhu king; it was decked with garlands of gold and was of the splendour of the rising sun.

verses.sanskrit: यथा देवासुरे युद्धे पुरा पूषा स्म शोभते। सौमदत्तेः पुनर्यूपो यज्ञशीलस्य धीमतः ॥२२॥
verses.english: With that device on his standard, Jayadratha appeared as beautiful. As Pusha in the days of yore, in the battle between the celestials and the Asuras.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजः सूर्य इवाभाति सोमश्चात्र प्रदृश्यते।  स यूपः काञ्चनो राजन् सौमद‌त्तेर्विराजते ॥२३॥
verses.english: The standard of Somadatta's son, ever devoted to the performance of sacrifices was decked with the device of a sacrificial stake. It shone like the sun or the moon.

verses.sanskrit: राजसूये मखश्रेष्ठे यथा यूपः समुच्छ्रितः।  शलस्य तु महाराज राजतो द्विरदो महान् ॥२४॥
verses.english: o king, that golden sacrificial stake decorating the banner of Somadatta's son, looked effulgent. Like the huge stake erected in that foremost of sacrifices, called the Rajasuya.

verses.sanskrit: केतुः काञ्चनचित्रांगैर्मयूरैरुपशोभितः।  स केतुः शोभयामास सैन्यं ते भरतर्षभ ॥२५॥
verses.english: Shalya's standard bearing the device of a silver-elephant, О king, as adorned on all sides with peacocks made of gold. O foremost of the

verses.sanskrit: यथा श्वेतो महानागो देवराजचमूं तथा।  नागो मणिमयो राज्ञो ध्वजः कनकसंवृतः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Like the prodigious white elephant adorning the host of the ruler of the celestials. On the gold-decked standard of king Duryodhana, was the device of an elephant embossed with gems.

verses.sanskrit: किंकिणीशतसंह्रादो भ्राजंश्चित्रो रथोत्तमे।  व्यभ्राजत भृशं राजन् पुत्रस्तव विशांपते ॥२७॥
verses.english: O king, that standard stood on the chariot of that hero, tinkling with the sound of a hundred bells. Then O monarch, in that battle with that huge standard, that foremost of the Kurus viz., your son appeared highly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजेन महता संख्ये कुरूणामृषभस्तदा।  नवैते तव वाहिन्यामुच्छ्रिताः परमध्वजाः ॥२८॥
व्यदीपयंस्ते पृतनां युगान्तादित्यसन्निभाः।  दशमस्त्वर्जुनस्यासीदेक एव महाकपिः ॥२९॥
verses.english: These nine excellent standards rose high amidst your troops and they lighted up your army, even like the suns that rise at the end of a Yuga.

verses.sanskrit: अदीप्यतार्जुनो येन हिमवानिव वह्निना।  ततश्चित्राणि शुभ्राणि सुमहान्ति महारथाः ॥३०॥
verses.english: The tenth standard there, was the mighty ape belonging to Arjuna with that standard Arjuna looked like a mountain lighted up by fire.

verses.sanskrit: कार्मुकाण्याददुस्तूर्णमर्जुनार्थे परन्तपाः।  तथैव धनुरायच्छत् पार्थः शत्रुविनाशनः ॥३१॥
verses.english: Then many mighty car-warriors all afflicters of their foes, quickly took up, for opposing Arjuna, their huge, white and variegated bows.
verses.bhavadeepa: हिमवानिव वह्निनेति तत्र किल पराशरेण वह्निः स्थापितः ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: गाण्डीवं दिव्यकर्मा तद्राजन्दुर्मन्त्रिते तव।  तवापराधाद्राजानो निहता बहुशो युधि ॥३२॥
verses.english: So also Pritha's son of godly achievements took up his bow capable of slaughtering the foe, namely the Gandiva; and all this was owing to your crooked policy.

verses.sanskrit: नानादिग्भ्यः समाहूताः सहयाः सरथद्विपाः।  तेषामासीद्व्यतिक्षेपो गर्जतामितरेतरम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Through your fault, in that battle, were slain numerous kings, invited from various countries, with their steeds and elephants and chariots.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनमुखानां च पाण्डूनामृषभस्य च।  तत्राद्भुतं परं चक्रे कौन्तेयः कृष्णसारथिः॥३४॥
verses.english: Then roaring at one another they fall upon one another, headed as they were by Duryodhana on one side and by that foremost of the Pandavas on the other.

verses.sanskrit: यदेको बहुभिः सार्धं समागच्छदभीतवत्।  अशोभत महाबाहुर्गाण्डीवं विक्षिपन् धनुः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Adorned with precious ornaments, graceful, possessing eyes of coppery hue, wearing round the head a tiara of gold radiant like the flames of fire, the mighty armed Sudakshina, the prince of the Kambojas, felled by Partha with his arrows, and lying dead on the ground, appeared beautiful like a charming hill with a flat summit.

verses.sanskrit: जिगीषुस्तान्नरव्याघ्रो जिघांसुश्च जयद्रथम्।  तत्रार्जुनो नरव्याघ्रः शरैर्मुक्तैः सहस्रशः ॥३६॥
verses.english: Then that mighty armed one appeared beautiful stretching his bow Gandiva desirous of defeating those best of men ranged against him and of slaughtering Jayadratha the ruler of the Sindhus.

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यांस्तावकान् योधान् प्रचक्रे शत्रुतापनः।  ततस्तेऽपि नरव्याघ्राः पार्थं सर्वे महारथाः ॥३७॥
verses.english: That foremost of men, that scorcher of his foes, viz., Arjuna discharging his arrows by thousands, made all the soldiers of your army invisible.

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यं समरे चक्रुः सायकौघैः समन्ततः।  संवृते नरसिंहैस्तु कुरूणामृषभेऽर्जुने।  महानासीत् समुद्भूतस्तस्य सैन्यस्य निःस्वनः ॥३८॥
verses.english: Thus when that foremost of the Kurus Arjuna had been surrounded by those foremost of men, the uproar that was raised in your army was indeed very great and deafening. of men, the uproar that was raised in your army was indeed very great and deafening.
